A header filter also dropped valid chromosome identifiers
A digits-only regex precedes an inner join; the run explicitly accepts 18 rows although its input has 20 chromosome groups.
Assert preservation of eligible chromosome identifiers and row counts across the join.
Luna Galaxy r1 explicitly asserts 20 rows and retains W and Z.
One scored-incorrect primary run with traced row loss; not a validation-absence rate.
Tool binding matched the request; scientific correctness depends on the requested filter.
Read-end artifacts were interpreted as a biological allele
Wrong-run exemplars report the pileup-based genotype; correct Sol runs record a read-position hypothesis and a Galaxy UDT that removes the apparent alternate signal.
Inspect allele support by read cycle and alignment end, rather than base quality alone.
Sol Galaxy r2/r3 execute a read-position audit inside Galaxy.
Twenty primary wrong calls attributed to the artifact by the targeted audit; this does not certify that all 20 omitted every validation step.
Domain judgment and validation rigor overlap; successful diagnostic use by Sol does not test the knowledge of other configurations.
GPT-5.5 code r1 first fits a held-out classifier, then replaces it with training-set estimates; GPT-5.5 Galaxy r1 fits and scores its estimators on the same reference reads.
Use grouped held-out or cross-fitted estimates and challenge perfect training separation.
Sol Galaxy r2 explicitly prevents identical reads from leaking between training and validation folds.
Two runs with in-sample leakage in the audit: one code and one Galaxy. A third wrong run follows a UDT outage and a different route.
The leakage mechanism is observed across both arms; the third wrong run is not counted as the same mechanism.
Structural plausibility or self-mapping was treated as sequence identity

A Galaxy run explicitly selects a circular, high-depth contig; a code run explicitly validates a seed by mapping reads back to that same seed. The three zero-score outputs share no canonical 31-mers with the workflow reference.
Test mitochondrial gene content or independent organellar identity, alongside structure, coverage and read support.
Successful Galaxy runs use the MitoHiFi reference-finding and assembly route.
Three zero-agreement candidates, one Galaxy and two code, attributed to non-mitochondrial candidate selection in the targeted audit.
The input-only policy conflicted with external-reference requirements. Some recorded validation was performed but did not establish molecular identity.
A direct cross-check contradicted the candidate identity but was not acted on
DeepSeek Galaxy r1 calls ENCODE peak-set overlap a direct identity check; its returned Jaccard values are approximately 0.0011 and 0.0006, yet it retains one of those candidates.
Treat negative candidate tests as reasons to broaden hypotheses and examine independent read-level evidence.
GPT-5.5 Galaxy r1 computes read-level promoter, gene-body and repeat enrichment with UDT jobs.
One direct ignored-cross-check example among two wrong DeepSeek Galaxy runs. The second has no reasoning transcript and is not counted as positive ignored-check evidence.
The audit also assigns domain-knowledge error. Weak overlap is evidence against the chosen candidate, not an independently definitive histone identity test.
